items.followUp: What is the role of chloroplasts in photosynthesis?

rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying chromoplasts as plastids containing coloured pigments.

rubric.why: Explains how flower colour helps pollination.
rubric.description: Links flower colour to attracting pollinators.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the colours attract pollinators, such as insects, and help pollination.

modelAnswer: Chromoplasts are plastids that contain coloured pigments and give colour to flowers and fruits.
The bright colours of flowers attract pollinators, such as insects, and help in pollination.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a threatened species and an extinct species.

rubric.why: Shows that an extinct species has no living members remaining.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that no living members of the species remain anywhere.

rubric.why: Distinguishes endangered species as still existing but at risk.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the species still exists but is at risk of extinction.

modelAnswer: An extinct species has no living members remaining anywhere on Earth.
An endangered species still exists but is at risk of becoming extinct.

items.followUp: Differentiate between reactants and products in a chemical reaction.

rubric.why: Identifies the substrate as the substance on which an enzyme acts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a substrate is the substance on which an enzyme or reaction acts.

rubric.why: Identifies the product as what the reaction forms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a product is the substance formed as a result of a reaction.

modelAnswer: A substrate is the substance on which an enzyme or chemical reaction acts.
A product is the substance formed as a result of the reaction.
